ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A circuit containing an ideal transformer is shown in the figure. In the figure, the resistance values of resistors R1, R2, and R3 are respectively 3Ω, 1Ω, and 4Ω; it is an ideal AC ammeter; U is a sinusoidal AC voltage source, and the effective value of the output voltage is constant. When switch S is open, the reading of the ammeter is I; when S is closed, the reading of the ammeter is 4I. The turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of this transformer is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A circuit containing an ideal transformer is shown in the figure. In the figure, the resistance values of resistors R1, R2 and R3 are respectively 3Ω, 1Ω, 4Ω, A is an ideal AC ammeter, U is a sinusoidal AC voltage source, and the effective value of the output voltage is constant. When switch S is open, the reading of the ammeter is I; when S is closed, the reading of the ammeter is 4I. What is the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of this transformer?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the circuit is a sinusoidal AC voltage source U, in series with the ideal AC ammeter A, resistor R1, and the primary coil of the transformer; the right side is the secondary coil of the transformer, and in its external circuit R2 is on top and R3 is below, connected in series. The branch of switch S is connected between the intermediate node of R2 and R3 and the lower-end node, so when S is closed it will short-circuit R3, and when S is open R2 and R3 are in series as the secondary-side load. Reasoning: Let the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the transformer be a=N1/N2. The problem gives R1=3Ω, R2=1Ω, R3=4Ω. When S is open, the secondary-side load is R2+R3=1+4=5Ω, converted to the primary side as a^2·5, so the total equivalent resistance seen by the power source is 3+5a^2. When S is closed, R3 is short-circuited, the secondary-side load is R2=1Ω, converted to the primary side as a^2·1, so the total equivalent resistance is 3+a^2. The effective value of the power source is constant, and the ammeter reading changes from I to 4I, so the current when closed is 4 times that when open: U/(3+a^2)=4·U/(3+5a^2), that is, (3+5a^2)/(3+a^2)=4. Solving gives 3+5a^2=12+4a^2, so a^2=9, and a takes the positive value 3.
